legacy_root.title: Hunt the negative results on multi-agent debate: where it does NOT beat a single model
legacy_root.question: Which published studies find multi-agent debate performing at or below a single well-prompted model, on what task types, and does the negative evidence explain the 05-ECO reject of 'multi-round free-form debate to consensus'?

all:"Should we be going MAD"

query_set.note: Title-string search for Du et al. with hyphenated 'Multi-Agent' returned 0; recovered by arXiv id because the paper titles it 'Multiagent Debate'.

retrieval_ratio.interpretation: Positive-verb search (Q-POS-BROAD-IMPROVE) returned 155 hits; explicit-null search (Q-NEG-UNDERPERFORM) returned 3 hits (ratio 155/3). Among the 83 unique papers retrieved by the mixed single-agent/CoT query, keyword classification labelled 44 POSITIVE vs 1 NEGATIVE — a positive-phrasing search buries nulls.

negative_result_register.title: Rethinking the Bounds of LLM Reasoning: Are Multi-Agent Discussions the Key?
negative_result_register.protocol: Liang-style MAD (3 agents, forced disagreement) vs single agent with demonstration
negative_result_register.strongest_caveat: MAD is not uniformly below: GSM8K Direct MAD 74 vs single 69. The at-or-below finding is for a *well-prompted* (demo) single agent, which is the comparison the unit asked for.

negative_result_register.title: Should we be going MAD? A Look at Multi-Agent Debate Strategies for LLMs
negative_result_register.protocol: default Multi-Persona MAD vs single agent and vs non-debate Medprompt
negative_result_register.effect_size_note: Multi-Persona MedQA 0.58 vs Single Agent 0.6 vs Medprompt 0.65
negative_result_register.strongest_caveat: Default MAD trails; Smit §3 then shows ~15% MedQA lift for Multi-Persona after agreement-intensity tuning, so the null is for off-the-shelf debate, not for every MAD hyperparameter.

negative_result_register.title: Stop Overvaluing Multi-Agent Debate -- We Must Rethink Evaluation and Embrace Model Heterogeneity
negative_result_register.effect_size_note: SoM MMLU 74.73 vs CoT 80.73; MP MATH 51.87 vs CoT 72.87; MAD win rate vs CoT ≤20% of 36 scenarios

win_rate_vs_cot.claim: none of these MAD methods achieve a win rate higher than 20% when compared to CoT across 36 scenarios (4 models × 9 benchmarks)
none of these MAD methods achieve a win rate higher than 20% when compared to CoT across 36 scenarios (4 models × 9 benchmarks)

negative_result_register.strongest_caveat: SoM GSM8K 94.93 vs CoT 93.60 is a within-paper counter-cell. Zhang also reports Heter-MAD as a fix (Table 4), so the null is for homogeneous default MAD vs a prompted single agent.

negative_result_register.title: When and Why Does Multi-Agent Debate Fail and Does It Really Underperform?
negative_result_register.protocol: consensus-seeking MAD (CosMAD / Du-style debate-to-consensus) vs single agent
negative_result_register.effect_size_note: CosMAD Avg F2 75.4 vs GPT4o-mini SA 82.2; CopMAD 57.34; CopMAD+DeepSeek-R1 24.89
negative_result_register.strongest_caveat: ColMAD Avg F2 86.29 vs SA 82.20 is an above-baseline counter-protocol. The 05-ECO reject names free-form debate *to consensus*, which is CosMAD, not ColMAD.

negative_result_register.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
negative_result_register.strongest_caveat: Headline-only: this hunt did not re-tabulate Du et al. numbers, so it cannot promote a mechanism. Recorded because the positive title-string query returned 0 hits (hyphenation Multiagent vs Multi-Agent) — a search-bias exhibit.

eco_reject.verdict_reason: The original 05-ECO paragraph at lines 97-103 is not on this Linux worktree, so the reject text cannot be quoted. The catalog names the reject as 'multi-round free-form debate to consensus'. That protocol matches consensus-seeking MAD (Du-style CosMAD): Chen et al. Table 1 show CosMAD Avg F2 75.40 vs GPT4o-mini single-agent 82.20 (−6.80) on error detection, and Wang et al. Table 2 show Liang-style MAD average-with-demo 70.04 vs a demonstrated single agent 75.63 (−5.59) on ECQA/GSM8K/FOLIO. Those numbers explain rejecting *untuned multi-round free-form debate-to-consensus* as a default. They do not explain a blanket ban on all multi-agent interaction: Smit's agreement-intensity Multi-Persona and Zhang's Heter-MAD can beat strong single-agent baselines once hyperparameters or model heterogeneity are introduced.
eco_reject.strongest_caveat: 05-ECO lines 97-103 were not readable here; the corroboration is of the catalog-named phrase, not of the unseen paragraph. Tuned or heterogeneous MAD is a documented counter-case (Smit Fig. 1 red cross; Zhang Table 4 Heter-SoM vs CoT-Average +5.8%).

reviewers.scope: Wang Table 2 and Chen Table 1 only. Did not see Smit or Zhang.
reviewers.finding: On this half: Liang-style MAD with demonstrations sits below a demonstrated single agent (70.04 vs 75.63 avg), and CosMAD sits below SA on error-detection F2 (75.40 vs 82.20). That is the free-form debate-to-consensus failure mode.

reviewers.scope: Smit Table 2 and Zhang Table 3 / Figure 1 only. Did not see Wang or Chen.
reviewers.finding: On this half: default Multi-Persona MedQA 0.58 vs single 0.60 vs Medprompt 0.65; SoM MMLU 74.73 vs CoT 80.73; MAD win rate vs CoT ≤20% of 36 scenarios. Default MAD does not beat a well-prompted single model on these tasks.
